module purpose: This block implements an XLEN-wide register array. It writes rd_i into a selected internal array entry on clock edges according to control-bus fields, drives two registered read outputs from selected entries, and optionally drives a third registered read output; with RST_EN enabled it also clears stored entries and rs1_o/rs2_o when rstn_i is low.

use-case flows.value: input data word rd_i written into a selected register-array entry
first read-output word taken from a selected register-array entry
second read-output word taken from a selected register-array entry
optional third read-output word taken from a selected register-array entry, otherwise forced to zero when disabled
stored entries and rs1_o/rs2_o cleared when RST_EN and rstn_i is low; entry 0 held at zero in the resettable build

conceptual assets.concept: Register-array data words held in the internal file and returned on the read outputs
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module's data input rd_i is copied into the internal array on qualified writes (`reg_file(...) <= rd_i;`, lines 86 and 110), and the stored array values are then sourced to the outputs from reg_file (`rs1_o` at lines 88 and 126, `rs2_o` at lines 89 and 127, and `rs3_o` at line 141 when RS3_EN; line 149 ties rs3_o to zero otherwise). Integrity is Established because these outputs are the values this entity delivers, so corrupt stored state or a wrong update breaks the implemented write/read relation. Availability is also Established because reg_file is edge-stored and, in the resettable build, the RTL defines recovery to zero on rstn_i low (lines 106-107, 117, 122-124).

conceptual assets.concept: Register-array write access decision — whether rd_i is written and which entry is targeted
conceptual assets.reasoning: The write flow computes and uses an internal decision about updating state. In the `not RST_EN` build, `rf_we <= (ctrl_i.rf_wb_en and (not rd_zero)) or ctrl_i.rf_zero_we;` (line 77) and `opa_addr <= "00000" when (ctrl_i.rf_zero_we = '1') else ctrl_i.rf_rd when (ctrl_i.rf_wb_en = '1') else ctrl_i.rf_rs1;` (lines 78-80) feed the write `if (rf_we = '1') then reg_file(...opa_addr...) <= rd_i;` (lines 85-86). In the `RST_EN` build, the direct condition at line 109 decides whether `reg_file(i) <= rd_i;` executes at line 110. Integrity is Established because this decision determines whether the stored state changes and which entry changes; corruption causes a missing write, a spurious write, or an update of the wrong entry. Availability is also Established under the RTL-visible condition that the implemented write predicates hold at a rising edge, because one selected entry is then updated.
